title: m2w-plan (plan.json)
description: How the runtime drives the graphs: the graph VARIANTS (KV protocol x compute type x staging rows) with, per variant, which graph for which phase / max length / chunk, which weights feed which half of a layer, and the profile the weights were built with.

profile.description: the GraphOptions the weights and all variants share (what differs between variants is in `variants`)

variants.description: the graph sets of the package; weights are shared by all of them. The runtime picks one (default: default_variant) when a session is created

id.description: staged-r<rows>-<compute type> | onehot-<compute type> | tensorScatter-<compute type> | scatterND-<compute type>; the graphs are in graphs/<id>/

compute_type.description: type of the computation inside the graphs; the boundaries stay float16

staging_rows.description: staged only: rows of the staging buffer = decode steps between flushes

scatter_index_type.description: tensorScatter only: data type of kv_write_index

value_layout.description: layout of the value cache: natural [1,kvHeads,P,128] (default) or transposed [1,kvHeads,128,P] (onehot variants); a transposed variant has an attention_guard output in its prefill graphs

block_group_controls.description: block groups: rope_cos / rope_sin / attention_mask shared by all blocks (models with one layer type) or declared per block as b<j>_rope_cos ... (hybrid models)

blocks_per_graph.description: decode block groups the package contains

recommended.description: the session options the model family runs best with (decode blocks per graph ...): the runtime and the pages use them when the caller does not choose

weights.description: tensor names of the weights manifest by the half of the layer they feed: a graph input with such a name is bound to that tensor of the layer

graphs.description: variant id -> the graphs of that variant

block_groups.description: number of blocks -> graph with that many blocks (hybrid-layer models: b<j>_ controls per block when block_group_controls = per_block); Gemma 4 (decode only): number of blocks per graph -> the schedule of the N - 1 blocks (see chain.block_groups)

key.description: the kinds of the blocks joined by '-' (so / fo / ss / fs)

chain.description: documentation of the dispatch chain (HEAD, BLOCK i = ffn of layer i + attention of layer i+1, TAIL, lm_head)

kv_protocols.description: documentation of how the KV cache is written and attended, by kv_style (the executable form is protocol.py / protocol.ts)
